description: Source of truth for the capabilities skills may call. Skills name a capability; the agent resolves it to the cawplan CLI or the CawPlan MCP server. Edit this file, then run: python3 scripts/capabilities.py render

activities.query.summary: Query the CawPlan activity feed (release, issue, ticket, version, product and user events), filtered by actor user_id and/or product_id over a relative time_range such as 1d, 1w, 1m, 3m, 6m or 1y. Paginated (page_size at most 100).

args.activity_types: body.activity_types (array of RELEASE, ISSUE, TICKET, VERSION, PRODUCT, USER)

backlog.attachments.download.summary: Download a backlog ticket's attachments to a local directory, optionally only some types or keys. CLI only (writes local files); on MCP, list the attachments and give the user the download URLs.

backlog.attachments.list.summary: List the files attached to a backlog ticket's rich-text fields, each with a short-lived presigned download URL (expires_in seconds, default 900, max 3600).

backlog.create.summary: Create a ticket in a product's backlog. description is the title; remarks is the HTML body. module_id: the CLI takes a module name, full path "Parent / Child" or id and resolves it; on MCP pass the module id (resolve a name with qa.module_tree.get first).

backlog.get.summary: Get one backlog ticket's full detail. ticket_id is the ticket unique ID (resolve a display ID with tickets.search first).

backlog.list.summary: List a product's backlog tickets (tickets not planned into a version). Paginated.

config.env.summary: Show the CLI's current CawPlan environment as plain text lines (Environment, API, Portal); the Portal line is the host used to build links. CLI only.

critical.search.summary: Search critical issues across products. Give a time window (time_range, or start_date with end_date); the other filters narrow it. Paginated.

knowledge.browse.summary: Interactive terminal browser (dataset, document, heading tree). Never run it as an agent: it needs a real terminal. Give the user the CLI example to run themselves. CLI only.

knowledge.datasets.create.summary: Create a knowledge dataset. owner_product_id makes that product the owner (required for its modules); product_ids only links the dataset for product-scoped search (CLI: repeat --product). CLI only.

knowledge.datasets.list.summary: List knowledge datasets visible to the caller ({id, name, document_count}). With product_id: the datasets that product owns plus those linked to it. With product_id and module_id: only the product's owned datasets with at least one document under that module.

knowledge.documents.get.summary: Get the raw content of one knowledge document (knowledge.search returns passages only). CLI-only options: outline (heading tree with per-heading preview, no content), section (complete content of the headings whose title contains the text), grep + context (matching lines with context), output (also save the full content to a file), refresh (bypass the local cache), no_interactive (plain JSON output even at a terminal). On MCP the full content is returned; find headings and sections in it yourself.

knowledge.documents.job_status.summary: Check an asynchronous upload or update job. CLI only.

knowledge.documents.list.summary: List the documents in one knowledge dataset.

knowledge.documents.set_module.summary: Move a document under a module (module_id) or out of its module (clear); pass exactly one. CLI only.

knowledge.documents.update.summary: Replace an existing document's content. CLI route: from a local file (file) or local text file (text_file). MCP route: from inline text (text); the document is re-indexed.

knowledge.documents.upload.summary: Upload local files (files, repeat --file) or local text files (text_files, repeat --text-file) into a dataset, optionally under a module of the dataset's owner product. Do not mix files and text_files in one call. File uploads are asynchronous; the CLI waits unless no_wait is set. CLI only (needs local files).

knowledge.modules.create.summary: Create a module (parent_id for a sub-module; at most 5 levels) in a product's module tree. CLI only.

knowledge.modules.list.summary: List a product's module tree; each node's knowledge lists the datasets with at least one document under it. CLI only for now.

knowledge.search.summary: Semantic search over knowledge datasets; returns ranked passages, not whole documents. Searches every accessible dataset unless dataset_ids narrows it (CLI: repeat --dataset per id).

labels.list.summary: List ticket labels; resolve label names to label IDs.

metrics.domains.summary: List key-metric domains and their metrics. MCP only: on the CLI route pick the domain from the metrics skill instead.

metrics.ingest.summary: Record business key-metric events (all or nothing: one invalid item rejects the batch). Each item: domain (default `default`), metric, at least one of value/count/cost/credit, dimensions.product (the product unique id), optional tags and timestamp. CLI-only: product_id fills dimensions.product on every item; on MCP set it on each item yourself.

metrics.query.summary: Query business key metrics for one domain over a time window (RFC3339 start inclusive, end exclusive). tag filters by key:value (repeat the CLI option once per tag); include_descendants needs module_id and product_id. CLI-only: chart and png write an SVG/PNG chart file (chart_field picks the plotted field); preview prints a terminal image and is for people running the CLI themselves.

product_lines.list.summary: List product lines; resolve a product line name to product_line_id.

products.analytics.summary: Get one product's AI-categorized feedback analytics over a time range, optionally for one version.

products.list.summary: List products visible to the caller; resolve a product name to product_id. MCP only: view=compact drops description, icon, links, knowledge datasets and member rosters; use it whenever you list more than a few products, and read one product's members (members.qas, members.designers, ...) with the default full view.

products.overview.summary: Get one product's overview (name and description background).

products.report.summary: Get a product's activity report for a date range (YYYY-MM-DD), optionally for one version.

qa.module_tree.get.summary: Get a product's module tree; its node IDs scope QA requirements and test points. MCP only: expand = requirements or approvers adds that data to each node. CLI route: the result is wrapped as {outcome, command, meta, data}; read the payload from `data` (outcome is SUCCESS or FAILURE).

qa.requirements.create.summary: Create a structured QA requirement under a module-tree node (body: module_tree_node_id, summary, entry_trigger, function_description, normal_expectation, constraints, out_of_scope, related_tickets, ...). CLI route: the result is wrapped as {outcome, command, meta, api, post_body|patch_body}; read the Open API envelope from `api`. outcome is SUCCESS, FAILURE, NOOP (nothing to change) or UNKNOWN (the write may or may not have happened: do not retry it, check with a read first). CLI-only: dry_run prints the body without sending it. CLI-only: body_file passes the same JSON from a file instead of body; prefer it for long JSON and where quoted arguments are rejected.

qa.requirements.get.summary: Get one QA requirement by its ID. CLI route: the result is wrapped as {outcome, command, meta, data}; read the payload from `data` (outcome is SUCCESS or FAILURE).

qa.requirements.list.summary: List QA requirements under a module-tree node (module_tree_node_id; the CLI requires it). MCP only: version_id, review_status, search and paging narrow the list, and module_tree_node_id may be omitted. CLI route: the result is wrapped as {outcome, command, meta, data}; read the payload from `data` (outcome is SUCCESS or FAILURE).

qa.requirements.reconcile.summary: Read-only check after a requirement create or update returned outcome UNKNOWN: finds whether the write landed, from local probe files. CLI only. On MCP no write returns UNKNOWN; if a call fails without a clear answer, look for the record with qa.requirements.list or qa.requirements.get before retrying.

qa.requirements.resolve.summary: Get a QA requirement by its display ID (for example REQ-00115) without knowing the product. The CLI also accepts a Browse URL; on MCP pass the display ID (take it from the URL first). CLI route: the result is wrapped as {outcome, command, meta, data}; read the payload from `data` (outcome is SUCCESS or FAILURE).

qa.requirements.testpoints.list.summary: List the test points of one QA requirement. CLI route: the result is wrapped as {outcome, command, meta, data}; read the payload from `data` (outcome is SUCCESS or FAILURE).

qa.requirements.update.summary: Update a QA requirement's structured fields. CLI route: pass desired (the full desired state) and snapshot (the values last written to CawPlan); the CLI sends only the keys that changed, outcome NOOP means nothing changed. MCP route: get the requirement first, stop and ask the user if a key you are changing differs from your snapshot, then send only the changed keys as desired. CLI route: the result is wrapped as {outcome, command, meta, api, post_body|patch_body}; read the Open API envelope from `api`. outcome is SUCCESS, FAILURE, NOOP (nothing to change) or UNKNOWN (the write may or may not have happened: do not retry it, check with a read first). CLI-only: dry_run prints the patch body without sending it. CLI-only: desired_file and snapshot_file pass the same JSON from files.

qa.risk_assessment.compute.summary: Compute a version's QA release risk assessment with the rule engine, without saving it; optionally scoped to one ticket or plan mappings. refresh_execution refreshes TestRail execution data first: the CLI does this by default (no_refresh_execution turns it off), on MCP pass refresh_execution=true. Needs QA Insights edit permission. CLI route: the result is wrapped as {outcome, command, meta, api}; read the Open API envelope {code, msg, data} from `api` (outcome is SUCCESS or FAILURE).

qa.risk_assessment.get.summary: Get the saved QA release risk assessment of a version. It reads the stored result and does not recompute it. CLI route: the result is wrapped as {outcome, command, meta, api}; read the Open API envelope {code, msg, data} from `api` (outcome is SUCCESS or FAILURE).

qa.risk_assessment.save.summary: Save a reviewed QA release risk assessment as the version's latest one (body: risk_level, reasons, note, ai_summary, override_rule_engine); each call adds a record, and the server writes an AI summary when ai_summary is omitted. CLI route: run it first with dry_run (prints the body, writes nothing), show the result to the user, and only after their confirmation run it again with confirm, the CLI's safety switch; never pass confirm on the first call. CLI route: the result is wrapped as {outcome, command, meta, api}; read the Open API envelope {code, msg, data} from `api` (outcome is SUCCESS or FAILURE). CLI-only: body_file passes the same JSON from a file instead of body; prefer it for long JSON and where quoted arguments are rejected. A dry_run call does not reach the server: it returns {outcome, command, meta, post_body} with no api.

qa.risk_rules.get.summary: Get a product's QA risk rules. CLI route: the result is wrapped as {outcome, command, meta, api}; read the Open API envelope {code, msg, data} from `api` (outcome is SUCCESS or FAILURE).

qa.testpoint_review.apply_optimization.summary: Apply the AI's {modified, added, questions} output to the review. Part of the local test point review page (served by the CLI on this machine). CLI only.

qa.testpoint_review.open.summary: Serve the review page and open it (no_browser prints the URL instead). Part of the local test point review page (served by the CLI on this machine). CLI only.

qa.testpoint_review.request_optimize.summary: Collect the reviewer's comments as an optimization request for the AI. Part of the local test point review page (served by the CLI on this machine). CLI only.

qa.testpoint_review.save.summary: Archive the reviewed test points to CawPlan for the requirement. dry_run prints the archive body without submitting. Part of the local test point review page (served by the CLI on this machine). CLI only.

qa.testpoint_review.show.summary: Show the current review state (test points, comments, decisions). Part of the local test point review page (served by the CLI on this machine). CLI only.

qa.testpoint_review.start.summary: Start a local test point review for a requirement from test points, the requirement snapshot and open questions (inline JSON or files); returns a review id. Part of the local test point review page (served by the CLI on this machine). CLI only.

qa.testpoints.archive.summary: Create several test points under one QA requirement (body: {test_points: [...]}). CLI route: the result is wrapped as {outcome, command, meta, api, post_body|patch_body}; read the Open API envelope from `api`. outcome is SUCCESS, FAILURE, NOOP (nothing to change) or UNKNOWN (the write may or may not have happened: do not retry it, check with a read first). CLI-only: body_file passes the same JSON from a file instead of body; prefer it for long JSON and where quoted arguments are rejected.

qa.testpoints.list.summary: List a product's QA test points, optionally narrowed by requirement, module-tree node, approval status, priority, assignee or keyword. Paginated. MCP only: this is the product-level list; the CLI's per-requirement test point list returns a different shape and is not a capability.

qa.testrail.execution.failures.summary: List the failed and blocked TestRail execution results of a version, optionally for one run. Paginated with limit and offset. include_flaky computes is_flaky and consecutive_failures from TestRail history (slower). CLI route: the result is wrapped as {outcome, command, meta, api}; read the Open API envelope {code, msg, data} from `api` (outcome is SUCCESS or FAILURE).

qa.testrail.execution.summary.summary: Get the TestRail execution summary of a version, optionally scoped to one ticket or to plan mappings. refresh bypasses the execution cache and refreshes TestRail status metadata. CLI route: the result is wrapped as {outcome, command, meta, api}; read the Open API envelope {code, msg, data} from `api` (outcome is SUCCESS or FAILURE).

qa.testrail.mappings.get.summary: Get a product's TestRail mappings. CLI route: the result is wrapped as {outcome, command, meta, api}; read the Open API envelope {code, msg, data} from `api` (outcome is SUCCESS or FAILURE).

qa_reports.create.summary: Create a QA report for a product version (body: topic, type, result, status, date_start, date_end, details, ticket_id, module_id, links, ...). CLI-only: body_file passes the same JSON from a file instead of body; prefer it for long JSON and where quoted arguments are rejected.

qa_reports.get.summary: Get one QA report of a version by its ID.

qa_reports.list.summary: List the QA reports of one product version, optionally filtered by type (sqa, aqa, stress, performance, smoke), result (pass, pass_with_issues, failed) or status. Paginated.

qa_reports.update.summary: Update an existing QA report (same body fields as qa_reports.create). CLI-only: body_file passes the same JSON from a file instead of body; prefer it for long JSON and where quoted arguments are rejected.

session.temp_dir.summary: Print the CLI's scratch directory for temporary files. It is a fixed directory shared by CLI sessions, so create a uniquely named subdirectory or file in it. CLI only.

ticket_statuses.list.summary: List one product line's ticket workflow statuses in order, including custom statuses.

tickets.attachments.add.summary: Upload local files (file, dir, md_file or html_file) and embed them, with an optional note, into one field of a version ticket (field, default progress_comment) in a single update. CLI only (reads local files). dry_run lists the files and missing references without uploading or updating. mode is append (default) or replace; block_id picks the report block to replace; base_dir, allow_outside_base and allow_outside_cwd control which local files may be referenced.

tickets.attachments.download.summary: Download a version ticket's attachments to a local directory, optionally only some types or keys. CLI only (writes local files); on MCP, list the attachments and give the user the download URLs.

tickets.attachments.list.summary: List the files attached to a version ticket's rich-text fields, each with a short-lived presigned download URL; fetch the URLs promptly. ticket_id is the ticket unique ID. Download, upload and add are separate CLI-only capabilities (tickets.attachments.download, .upload, .add).

tickets.attachments.upload.summary: Upload local files as a version ticket's attachments and return their keys and URLs (does not change the ticket text). CLI only (reads local files). dry_run lists what would be uploaded.

tickets.changes.summary: List ticket change events (status, ux, priority, assignees) in a window of at most 90 days for a scope (at least one of unique_ids, product_ids, product_line_ids, version_ids, parent_ids); at most 50 unique_ids per call. The CLI follows next_cursor for up to 20 pages; on MCP each call returns one page, so call again with cursor = next_cursor until there is none. truncated: true means the result is incomplete.

tickets.create.summary: Create a ticket in a product version. description is the title; remarks is the HTML body. For a ticket outside any version use backlog.create. module_id: the CLI takes a module name, full path "Parent / Child" or id and resolves it; on MCP pass the module id (resolve a name with qa.module_tree.get first).

tickets.get.summary: Get one version ticket's full detail (labels, children, parent, relations, product line, AI sessions, QA reports). ticket_id is the ticket unique ID (resolve a display ID with tickets.search first).

tickets.history.summary: Get one version ticket's change history.

tickets.relations.summary: List a ticket's relations grouped by type (blocking, blocked_by, related, duplicate), from that ticket's point of view. ticket_id is the ticket unique ID (resolve a display ID with tickets.search first).

tickets.search.summary: Find tickets by display ID, unique ID or filters. Returns full ticket fields, including description (title), remarks (body), progress_comment and links. A created-at window (time_range, or start_date + end_date) is required unless display_ids, unique_ids or parent_ids is set; updated_start_date/updated_end_date filter by last update. Paginated: page through using total. view=compact returns list fields only (IDs, description, status and status_display, priority, ux, product/version, parent, labels (name, behavior), assignees (user_id and name), qa_assignee_ids, module, dates) without rich text, links, relations or avatars; use tickets.get for one ticket's details. Use it whenever you list more than a few tickets: full rows are large enough to overflow a tool result. On the CLI it also prints one line per page and defaults page_size to 50; CLI releases before this change printed a reduced row without IDs.

tickets.stats.summary: Count tickets grouped server-side (priority, status, status_category, ux, assignee, label, type, product, version, platform; at most 2 dimensions), with the same filters as tickets.search. Result: data.total, and data.groups[] where each group has count and values[] (one {dimension, value} per group_by dimension).

tickets.update.summary: Update a version ticket's fields (status, progress_comment, priority, assignees, labels, parent, due date, title/body, BUGFIX root_cause and solution), or move it with target_version_id. ticket_id is the ticket unique ID. Pass the ticket's current version as expected_version to use the optimistic lock (0 or omitted skips the check). module_id: the CLI takes a module name, full path "Parent / Child" or id and resolves it; on MCP pass the module id (resolve a name with qa.module_tree.get first). On MCP, null or an empty string clears the module; omitting it keeps the module.

todos.list.summary: List one user's open work: assigned tickets and critical issues.

users.me.summary: Get the signed-in user (resolve "me" to user_id): data.unique_id is the user_id, with email and name. A not-signed-in error means the route is not usable: follow "Neither" above instead of looking the user up by email.

users.search.summary: Find users by exact email or by keyword over name and email; resolve a person to user_id. CLI route: do not pass page_size or page_num (the CLI sends them as strings and the server answers BAD_REQUEST); use email or keyword only.

versions.create.summary: Create a version in a product.

versions.get.summary: Get one version's detail (status, dates, completion, risk).

versions.list.summary: List one product's versions; resolve a version name to version_id.

versions.releases.summary: Get a version's release history. data is a list of version entries; the events are in each entry's release_history[].
